PocketRun Chapter 7 Linux candidate — license scope and distribution gate
Audit date: 2026-11-19
This is a source/compliance audit, NOT Chapter 7 device acceptance or permission to publish a binary.

1. Android App versus separate programs
PRoot is started as a separate ProcessBuilder child using command-line arguments, environment and byte pipes. It is not loaded by JNI/dlopen into the App. Packaging an executable under jniLibs with a .so filename does not turn that executable into an App-linked library.
On these facts, the App and PRoot are normally separate works in an aggregate (GPLv2 section 2; GPLv3 section 5). This does not automatically put unrelated Kotlin, React Native/JS or App code under GPL. A process boundary alone is not an absolute legal exemption: later shared-address-space linking, copied GPL code or intimate exchange of program-internal structures would require a new assessment. Distribution conditions must not restrict the individual GPL-covered programs' rights.

2. PRoot and talloc are a combined executable
PRoot v5.1.107.102 source headers permit GPL-2.0-or-later. The candidate statically links talloc 2.5.0, whose talloc.c/talloc.h headers permit LGPL-3.0-or-later. GPLv2-only is not an appropriate license claim for this combined executable. Exercise PRoot's later-version permission and distribute the combined PRoot executable under GPLv3; preserve talloc's LGPLv3-or-later notices and additional permissions. The separate PRoot loader also originates in GPL-2.0-or-later source; preserve its notices and corresponding source.
The full PRoot+talloc source archive, six-file adapter diff, generated replace.h and reproduction/build scripts are in matching_sources/proot-talloc/. The source archive SHA256 is eb5d7c20067c7c14e1ffb5047408a96270b95ae4682dd34bc80dc526252165ef. It was byte-reproduced by the candidate builder; this audit verifies its provenance/hashes and does not claim a new compilation or device run.
Full source and instructions for recompiling/relinking PRoot with a modified talloc are the relevant LGPLv3 section 4(d)(0) material. Android platform libraries not copied into the distribution are a distinct system-library question. An App source URL is not a substitute for this combined executable's source.

3. Do not call Alpine "MIT"
The fixed official Alpine minirootfs is 3.22.8/aarch64, SHA256 36091efacd083c1cf5a8c837272530bff4fc72db1fbfdef559f52de0d890bca4. Its installed database has 16 packages with distinct licenses. The original 17 guest ELF files are mapped individually in fixed-payload-inventory.json. BusyBox/apk-tools/scanelf are GPLv2-only; musl is MIT with third-party permissive notices; musl-utils contains BSD-2-Clause getconf/getent and GPLv2-or-later iconv; OpenSSL is Apache-2.0; zlib is Zlib; CA data includes MPL-2.0. Package-level metadata is not a license for every unrelated file or static dependency.

4. Full 19-ELF candidate is BLOCKED for public binary/rootfs distribution
The original apk-tools/libapk2 2.14.13-r0 and ssl_client 1.37.0-r20 are recorded as GPL-2.0-only and directly link distributed Apache-2.0 OpenSSL 3.5.9 libraries. The exact apk-tools source LICENSE and SPDX headers have no later-version grant; a scan of the collected exact source found no OpenSSL linking exception. ssl_client.c has no per-file grant or copyright header; its package grant is GPLv2-only. Do not invent an exception, relabel them GPLv3, or treat separately bundled OpenSSL as absent. The GPLv2 system-library exception explicitly excludes a component that itself accompanies the executable. Source delivery alone does not resolve incompatible licensing. Obtain applicable rights evidence or genuinely omit these linked works from the shipped scope.

5. Minimal variant can avoid that particular incompatibility
A precisely scoped variant retaining only the original BusyBox ELF and musl ELF plus PRoot and loader no longer distributes apk/libapk/ssl_client/OpenSSL. BusyBox's dynamic dependencies contain only musl; its static utmps/skalibs dependencies must still be included in the source and copyright inventory. Their ISC license is compatible with GPLv2. See MINIMAL-DISTRIBUTION.txt for the proposed scope, exact fixed hashes and data cleanup. This is conditional until the real minimal asset, bindings, APK contents, notices and source delivery are checked.

6. Public delivery is still NOT fulfilled by this local directory
GPLv2 section 3 and GPLv3 section 6 require the relevant Corresponding Source delivery mechanism. A notice with an upstream homepage URL, a private archive, a future Git commit, or a model-written report is not completed public source delivery. For Internet distribution, prefer equivalent-access, version-matched source archives alongside the binary at the designated distribution place (GPLv2 section 3 final paragraph; GPLv3 section 6(d)), with exact checksums and build/install/relink scripts. If GPLv3 source is hosted elsewhere, explicit directions and availability must satisfy section 6(d); GPLv2-only recipients still need equivalent source access from the same designated place. No three-year written source offer has been created or backed here.
This audit makes no claim that a GPLv3 User Product transaction occurred. Assess installation-information requirements if distribution is tied to transfer of a User Product. Keep instructions for modifying/rebuilding/re-signing/reinstalling the executable-bearing APK, where applicable, without disclosing a private signing key. A development test is not a substitute for those instructions or recipient access.

Authoritative text copies: licenses/GPL-2.0.txt, GPL-3.0.txt, LGPL-3.0.txt and component notices.
References: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html#MereAggregation
